header.text: People have lived in the territory of present-day Brazil for thousands of years. But in the 1500s, Portuguese sailors arrived there and claimed the land for Portugal. Since then, many people from all over the world have come to Brazil. Read the table about the history of people who have come to Brazil. Then follow the instructions below.

table.text: The Portuguese establish the village of São Vicente, the first permanent Portuguese settlement in South America.
More than four million people from Africa are enslaved and forced to work on Brazilian sugarcane plantations and in mines.
Brazil becomes independent from Portugal in 1822. The leader of Brazil encourages people from Central Europe to move to Brazil by offering them farmland.
The Brazilian government encourages people from countries in Southern Europe, such as Italy, to come to Brazil and work on Brazilian coffee plantations.
More people move to Brazil from countries such as Japan, Syria, and Lebanon.

header.text: People have lived in the territory of present-day Brazil for thousands of years. But in the 1500s, Portuguese sailors arrived there and claimed the land for Portugal. Since then, many people from all over the world have come to Brazil. Read the table about the history of people who have come to Brazil. Then follow the instructions below.

table.text: The Portuguese establish the village of São Vicente, the first permanent Portuguese settlement in South America.
More than four million people from Africa are enslaved and forced to work on Brazilian sugarcane plantations and in mines.
Brazil becomes independent from Portugal in 1822. The leader of Brazil encourages people from Central Europe to move to Brazil by offering them farmland.
The Brazilian government encourages people from countries in Southern Europe, such as Italy, to come to Brazil and work on Brazilian coffee plantations.
More people move to Brazil from countries such as Japan, Syria, and Lebanon.

contents.text: Since the 1960s, Brazil has continued to become more urban. Today, over 80% of people in Brazil live in cities. The rapid growth of Brazilian cities between the 1960s and today has created advantages and disadvantages for Brazilian people. Decide whether the statements below describe an advantage or a disadvantage of urbanization.

questions.text: Many cities have grown quickly. But sometimes, city governments do not have enough money to provide services to all new residents. So, some people may not have access to clean water or good healthcare.
Cities offer many job opportunities. So, people who move to cities may find work.

Cities don't have enough houses for everyone who moves there. As a result, newcomers are often forced to build their homes on the outskirts of cities. Often these homes are built quickly and can be unsafe.

Mexico City sits in a valley high in the mountains. This high elevation keeps the climate mild year-round. So, Mexico City does not get as hot or humid as parts of the country along the coast. Mexico City's location helped its population grow. The surrounding volcanic soil was an important natural resource. Today, Mexico City is the political, financial, and cultural center of Mexico. Many of the country's leaders work there, and it is home to many jobs, factories, and businesses.

contents.text: Read the passage about Mexico City. Then answer the question below.

title.text: Mexico City, Mexico, historical landmark Basilica of Our Lady of Guadalupe with Mexico City skyline

textContent.text: Mexico City is one of the largest cities in the world. It is in central Mexico, far from the ocean. About 22 million people live in and around Mexico City—that's about one-sixth of the whole country's population!

Mexico City sits in a valley high in the mountains. This high elevation keeps the climate mild year-round. So, Mexico City does not get as hot or humid as parts of the country along the coast. Since Mexico City is relatively close to the equator, it rarely faces the freezing temperatures that are typical of many other high-altitude places. This pleasant climate attracts people from all over Mexico to live and work there.

Mexico City's location helped its population grow. The surrounding volcanic soil was an important natural resource. Volcanic soil is very fertile, so farmers could grow enough food to feed a growing population. But the mountains around the city limit its expansion, so many people settled close together.
Today, Mexico City is the political, financial, and cultural center of Mexico. Many of the country's leaders work there, and it is home to many jobs, factories, and businesses.

choices.text: Its coastal location provides easy access to the Gulf of America's oil and fish.
Its elevation and location create a mild year-round climate that draws many people.
Its flat surroundings made it easy for the city to expand into a wider area.
Its fertile volcanic soil enabled early farmers to produce a large food supply.

contents.text: Read the passage about Mexico City. Then answer the question below.

title.text: Mexico City, Mexico, historical landmark Basilica of Our Lady of Guadalupe with Mexico City skyline

textContent.text: Mexico City is one of the largest cities in the world. It is in central Mexico, far from the ocean. About 22 million people live in and around Mexico City—that's about one-sixth of the whole country's population!

Mexico City sits in a valley high in the mountains. This high elevation keeps the climate mild year-round. So, Mexico City does not get as hot or humid as parts of the country along the coast. Since Mexico City is relatively close to the equator, it rarely faces the freezing temperatures that are typical of many other high-altitude places. This pleasant climate attracts people from all over Mexico to live and work there.

Mexico City's location helped its population grow. The surrounding volcanic soil was an important natural resource. Volcanic soil is very fertile, so farmers could grow enough food to feed a growing population. But the mountains around the city limit its expansion, so many people settled close together.
Today, Mexico City is the political, financial, and cultural center of Mexico. Many of the country's leaders work there, and it is home to many jobs, factories, and businesses.

contents.text: Based on the passage above, which sentence describes a geographic factor that helped Mexico City grow?

choices.text: Its poisonous volcanic soil protects the city from attackers.
Its high-altitude location results in a milder climate than other regions.
Its mountain climate causes freezing winters and humid summers.
Its coastal location provides easy access to the Pacific Ocean's seafood.

pieces.text: Brazil and Mexico use a form of government called a

. In both countries, citizens elect a president who serves as the head of the government. Just like in the United States, citizens in Brazil and Mexico also elect representatives to serve in Congress, making their country's laws. People can choose representatives from different political parties, meaning groups whose members share similar ideas about how to run a country. Mexico has several major parties, while Brazil has dozens!
Both countries also have a
, which is a set of fundamental laws for the nation. These constitutions protect important rights, such as the freedom of speech and the right to gather peacefully to share ideas.

contents.text: Cuba is an island nation in the Caribbean Sea. Cuba has a different form of government from Brazil and Mexico. Read the passage about Cuba's government. Then answer the question below.

pieces.text: Cuba's form of government is an

. It is called a one-party state because it has only one political party: the Communist Party of Cuba. It is illegal to start or join any other party, and the Cuban constitution even states that the Communist Party of Cuba must always control the government. All government officials belong to the Communist Party. People in Cuba vote to select many of their government leaders, but they can only choose candidates from the Communist Party.

textContent.text: The central government holds all the power in Cuba. It even makes local decisions, like controlling whether to fix potholes in neighborhood roads. So, the central government has a lot of control over daily life, including what people can say or read in the news. Cuba's constitution says that everyone has freedom of speech. But it is still illegal to criticize the government.

. It is called a one-party state because it has only one political party: the Communist Party of Cuba.
